message.content: The sea’s color isn’t fixed—it changes with depth, water composition, light conditions, and what’s floating in it. In clear, shallow waters you’ll often see turquoise or greenish hues because of dissolved organic matter and algae. In deeper, clearer waters the dominant effect is Rayleigh scattering of sunlight, giving the classic blue appearance. Near shorelines, sediment and plankton can tint the water brown, red, or even orange. So while “blue” is the most common description, the actual color can vary widely from green to turquoise to deep indigo depending on the environment.
